summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of repetitively pulsed laser radiation on the fabrication of Ti-6Al-4V-B4C metal-matrix composite via selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting with repetitively pulsed laser was employed to fabricate the composite.
summary_en.result: Pulsed laser processing enhanced the microstructure and mechanical properties of the composite.
summary_en.validation: Validation through material characterization including SEM and hardness testing.

papers.title: Radiographic Evaluation of Bone Remodeling after Additively Manufactured Subperiosteal Jaw Implantation (AMSJI) in the Maxilla: A One-Year Follow-Up Study.
papers.abstract: Additively manufactured subperiosteal jaw implants (AMSJI) are patient-specific, 3D-printed, titanium implants that provide an alternative solution for patients with severe maxillary bone atrophy. The aim of this study was to evaluate the bony remodeling of the maxillary crest and supporting bone using AMSJI. Fifteen patients with a Cawood-Howell Class V or greater degree of maxillary atrophy were evaluated using (cone beam) computed tomography scans at set intervals: one month (T1) and twelve months (T2) after definitive masticatory loading of bilateral AMSJI implants in the maxilla. The postoperative images were segmented and superimposed on the preoperative images. Fixed evaluation points were determined in advance, and surface comparison was carried out to calculate and visualize the effects of AMSJITM on the surrounding bone. A total mean negative bone remodeling of 0.26 mm (SD 0.65 mm) was seen over six reference points on the crest. Minor bone loss (mean 0.088 mm resorption, SD 0.29 mm) was seen at the supporting bone at the wings and basal frame. We conclude that reconstruction of the severely atrophic maxilla with the AMSJI results in minimal effect on supporting bone. Reduced stress shielding with a biomechanically tuned subperiosteal implant does not induce radiographically significant crestal bone atrophy.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文评估下颌种植体周围的骨重塑，与髋关节植入物应力屏蔽及微动分析无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not quantify femoral stem stress shielding, micromotion, or bone-implant interface mechanics; it focuses on radiographic bone remodeling around maxillary implants, with no FEA, contact modeling, or comparison to intact femur.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估3D打印个性化下颌种植体对严重上颌骨萎缩患者骨重塑的影响。
summary_zh.method: 对15例患者术后CBCT扫描进行分割、叠加和表面比较，测量固定参考点处的骨变化。
summary_zh.result: 12个月后，牙槽嵴平均骨吸收0.26 mm，支持骨吸收0.088 mm，表明骨重塑影响最小。
summary_zh.validation: 临床随访研究，使用影像学方法（CBCT）进行骨变化定量分析。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the bone remodeling effect of additively manufactured subperiosteal jaw implants on severely atrophic maxillae.
summary_en.method: CBCT scans at 1 and 12 months post-loading were segmented, superimposed, and compared at predefined reference points to quantify bone changes.
summary_en.result: Minimal crestal bone resorption (mean 0.26 mm) and supporting bone resorption (mean 0.088 mm) were observed, indicating reduced stress shielding.
summary_en.validation: Clinical follow-up study with radiographic analysis using CBCT imaging and surface comparison.
